source.title: High-Dimensional Analysis of Gradient Flow for Extensive-Width Quadratic Neural Networks
source.authors: Simon Martin; Giulio Biroli; Francis R. Bach

record.file_problem: The supplied text is cut off during Appendix J.2.1. The main text and the relevant discussion of overfitting and double descent are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own quadratic-network results on test-error behavior over training time and sample complexity, and qualifies the findings by label noise and regularization. Its model and measurements differ from the original deep-network settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports MSE curves over time (Figure 6) and sample complexity (Figure 7). Values shown only in plots are recorded as figure only. It also compares its Gaussian surrogate and quadratic-network trajectories in Figure 13, but that comparison is not a result on one of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own results on test error in a new setting: a shallow quadratic teacher-student network trained by gradient descent, with matching DMFT long-time equations. Figure 7 shows MSE against sample complexity α peaking near the derived interpolation threshold, depending on label noise Δ and regularization λ. Figure 6 shows MSE against training time with overfitting. It is not an original source, and its method and measure differ from the original deep-network experiments, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, with additions. The authors show overfitting along GD dynamics, already present without noise and amplified by noise. With label noise, their long-time equations and GD simulations show double descent in MSE versus sample complexity. The peak coincides with the interpolation threshold derived in the λ→0+ limit, and the peak is reduced by stronger λ in the tested range. They present this as the first explicit dynamical characterization of double descent in a nonlinear high-dimensional model. They admit they cannot precisely characterize when it occurs; small Δ shows none.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes gradient descent in a teacher–student shallow quadratic network, using MSE and sample complexity α; it does not reproduce the original deep-network size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported overfitting and double-descent behavior varies with label-noise variance Δ and regularization strength λ; the authors say small noise values may not produce double descent and stronger regularization reduces overfitting in the plotted range.

fits_no_version.finding: Overfitting along GD dynamics (final MSE above the time-minimum) already appears with no label noise. It is amplified by noise and grows with α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In gradient-trained networks, the overfitting gap during training grows with sample complexity and label noise.

record.problems: The high-dimensional dynamics and long-time results rely partly on non-rigorous assumptions; the authors say the steady-state assumptions are not proved. Relevant double-descent results are numerical, with plotted values rather than tabulated measurements; simulations use finite dimension and are averaged over 10 realizations in Figure 7.

untested.parts: There is no model-size sweep showing a peak at the interpolating width. A κ dependence is discussed (larger κ gives lower training loss and higher MSE), but not as a fall-rise-fall curve.
A second descent in time after the overfitting rise, and the location of an epoch-wise threshold.
Risk improving again as capacity (rather than sample size) passes the interpolation point, and the claim across model classes.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting the peak on several axes. Only the sample axis is tested, where the peak coincides with the theoretically derived α_inter(κ,κ*,Δ).
Whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak; only a range of λ values is tested. Triple or multiple descent is not tested.
Re-plotting against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Unregularized GD at κ=0.7, κ*=0.5, Δ=0.5. Below α_inter, training loss is zero and in-sample error is Δ/4. Above α_inter, MSE and in-sample error fall despite rising training loss; the second descent appears without regularization.
Statement that the MSE peak coincides with the λ→0+ interpolation threshold α_inter, derived in Proposition 6.
κ sweep near κ*: larger κ gives lower training loss but higher MSE, more so at small λ.
Double-descent regime curves of MSE and in-sample error.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The theory relies on non-rigorous DMFT and steady-state assumptions and a Gaussian-equivalence conjecture, but GD simulations (d=100, averaged over 10 runs) match the equations closely. The double descent is along the sample axis, not model size. For V2, the study's own definition of overfitting (δMSE = MSE∞ − inf_t MSE(t) > 0) shows a fall-rise with no recovery, which argues against a full epoch-wise double descent in this setting. The text was cut in Appendix J, so Figures 17–20 were not fully seen.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and peak near the training-set interpolation size.
The study reports time-dependent MSE and overfitting, but does not establish a full fall-rise-fall epoch-wise curve or locate an epoch-wise interpolation threshold.
The sample-complexity sweep is at fixed student width; the study does not test whether more data hurts across model sizes or other model classes.
General double descent across model classes; the study analyzes a shallow quadratic network.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs and sample count.
The study tests label-noise and regularization dependence. It does not establish triple or multiple descent, or test whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
Whether using an effective parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.
